sc: School child, fever and anorexia, then jaundice, tender liver, ALT in thousands → Hepatitis A: anti-HAV IgM
Teenager with liver disease, tremor, Kayser–Fleischer rings → Wilson disease
Vomiting and coma after aspirin in varicella, no jaundice → Reye syndrome
f: Faeco-oral · never chronic · anti-HAV IgM · supportive · hepatitis E kills pregnant women
HBsAg = infection (> 6 months = chronic) · anti-HBc IgM = acute · anti-HBs alone = vaccinated
Baby of HBsAg+ mother: HBIG + vaccine within 12–24 h, then breastfeed · birth infection → 90% chronic
C: highest chronic rate, direct-acting antivirals 12 weeks · D needs HBsAg
INR ≥ 2 (≥ 1.5 with encephalopathy) · confusion · falling ALT is a bad sign · ICU, avoid sedatives
Wilson (low caeruloplasmin, penicillamine) · schistosomal portal hypertension (normal liver tests) · bleeding varices: band ligation
trap: PT/INR is the best test of liver injury severity, not ALT · no aspirin for children with viral illness (Reye) · hepatitis A and E never become chronic
